meta.title: The Splitter's Real Text Domain
meta.description: What Whisper emits, what the pipeline erases, what the splitter actually sees, and five ways to train for it

props.title: Do we have commas in our training data?
props.subtitle: Yes — and the pipeline guarantees the splitter never sees one
props.meta: 2026-08-15 · live pipeline trace receipts · v3 commission held pending your pick

props.content: Three measured facts. One: our frozen Whisper DOES emit commas — 96% of ASR rows have them — but it places them unreliably, including inside callsigns. Two: it writes numbers as digits 99% of the time ('runway 31', 'contact ground 121.9', 'number 5') while our training corpus spells every number out. Three — the decisive one: the pipeline's first cleanup stage applies punctuation-to-space before anything else runs, so by the time text reaches the compound-split seat at stage 8, every comma is gone. Your instinct was right where it matters: training a splitter on comma-anchored cuts teaches it a token that cannot exist at its seat. The real domain gap is commas AND numerals AND hyphens, and the fix list below addresses all three.

props.title: Case is free, and the preamble is a bonus finding
props.content: The BERT encoder is uncased, so uppercase costs nothing. The preamble row is the sleeper: the production seat receives text AFTER callsign stripping, so training blocks that include callsigns spend model capacity on a skill the seat never exercises — and the probe's cut indices were offset by preamble tokens the seat would not have. Seat-exact training also simplifies the corpus.

props.label: Five options
props.title: How we fix it
props.subtitle: All five keep the constituent-pool architecture, the alignment gate, and the lineage law. They differ in where the domain match happens.

props.title: 1 — Canonical-shape corpus
props.content: Pipe every generated block through the ACTUAL production normalizer (import canonical_text_normalizer, not a copy) at emit time, and emit command_text-shaped blocks with the preamble already stripped. Commas vanish from training exactly as they vanish at the seat; cut indices recompute after token deletion. Kills the comma crutch and the preamble waste in one move. Does NOT fix numerals on its own. Cost: small generator change + regeneration.

props.title: 2 — Dual numeral surfaces
props.content: Every block renders in both surface families: spoken words ('runway three one') and whisper digits ('RUNWAY 31', '121 9'), sharing one cut structure. The digit renderer is deterministic from the slot values already recorded in provenance — no new authority, no guessing. Mix at measured rates (digits ~99% on ASR lanes, words on clean lanes). Fixes the biggest gap; leaves commas in. Cost: a renderer + corpus grows or samples 50/50.

props.title: 3 — Seat-exact corpus (1 + 2) — RECOMMENDED
props.content: Both fixes together: canonical shape AND dual numeral surfaces. Training distribution equals the seat distribution by construction, and because the generator imports the pipeline's own normalizer, the two can never drift — a pipeline normalization change automatically re-shapes the next corpus. The probe reruns against command_text to give honest before/after numbers. Cost: the sum of 1+2, still one generator commission.

props.title: 4 — ASR round-trip slice
props.content: Push a sample of generated compounds through the real TTS + frozen-Whisper fixture machinery and keep Whisper's own output as training/eval text — real numeral habits, real comma hallucinations (pre-strip), real homophone noise. The only option that captures ASR ERRORS, not just ASR formatting. Use as the dev/test realism anchor plus an optional train slice. Cost: highest — audio synthesis + transcription time per row; run it on hundreds, not thousands.

props.title: 5 — Model-boundary invariance
props.content: Leave the corpus alone; make the SPM encode step canonicalize input for train AND inference alike (drop punctuation tokens, optionally map digit runs and spelled numbers to one shared representation). One choke point, no regeneration. But it hides real signal (digit spans and word spans have different lengths, which shifts slot boundaries), duplicates a normalization the pipeline already owns, and drifts from the seat contract. Cheapest, least honest — keep as fallback only.

props.title: Pick option 3, anchor with option 4
props.content: Seat-exact corpus (canonical shape + dual numeral surfaces, preamble-stripped command_text blocks) as the v3 data spec, with an ASR round-trip slice of a few hundred rows as the dev/test realism anchor. Option 5 stays a fallback if regeneration cost ever becomes the constraint. The v3 scale-up agent was stopped mid-run by the earlier session exit and is NOT re-dispatched — its commission changes materially under any option here, so it waits for your pick. Its partial on-disk corpus is unvalidated; the next full run overwrites it deterministically.
